text:
kevin: Heads up — on a private VPC node I'm seeing ~2-3ms higher median but a ~30-40ms bump in 99p for short-gen workloads when running in containerd vs host network. Suspect NIC offload + container network stack interaction. Can someone run a quick microbench and confirm?

kevin: Repro steps (should be quick, 1m):
```
# on the target private node (dc2-node-18)
# 1) baseline: host network
sudo ethtool -k eth0 | egrep 'generic|large'
wrk -t2 -c50 -d60s http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/generate

# 2) container (default bridge)
docker run --rm -p 8080:8080 my-test-image:sha12345 &
wrk -t2 -c50 -d60s http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/generate

# 3) toggle offloads (host)
sudo ethtool -K eth0 gro off gso off tso off
# rerun host network wrk
```

kevin: If you can also capture `cat /proc/interrupts` and `sudo journalctl -u containerd --since "-2m"` that'd help. @anna can you take node dc2-node-18? :eyes:

anna: I can do a quick pass in 10m. which commit/model should I use?

kevin: Use image `redwood/runtime-test:sha12345` (same as daily). Endpoint is the internal test route `/api/generate` with short prompts.

sachin: Also please check irqbalance and CPU isolation. If interrupts are moving around it can blow p99. Quick commands: `ps -eLo pid,psr,cmd | grep containerd` and `taskset -p <pid>` to see affinity.

maria: FWIW we saw similar when switching from host to cni-plugin x -> it was GRO causing larger coalesced packets and a single CPU doing large batch work. Disabling GRO helped in that case for tail latency.

anna: running baseline host now. attaching quick outputs.
```
# host baseline wrk summary
Latency   2.3ms    95%  8.7ms   99%  18.4ms
Requests/sec: 12.5k

# /proc/interrupts (snippet)
           CPU0       CPU1       CPU2       CPU3
eth0:     124523      2345     10234       120
```

anna: container (bridge) run completed:
```
Latency   4.7ms    95%  12.5ms  99%  52.1ms
Requests/sec: 11.8k
journalctl shows containerd logs spiking around time X with ENOBUFS warnings
```

jonathan: Noted. Can you flip off GRO/GSO/TFO on host and rerun (kevin's step 3)? Also check `netstat -s | grep retransmit` to see if there are TX issues.

anna: flipped offloads, reran host:
```
Latency   2.6ms    95%  9.2ms   99%  19.1ms
Requests/sec: 12.3k
```

anna: So host with offloads off ~= baseline. Container bridge still has high 99p.

sachin: That indicates container path + bridge/NAT is adding jitter. Two quick experiments: (1) run container with `--network host` (no bridge) to see if container runtime alone causes it, (2) try `--net=containerd` or use CNI `macvlan`/host-device.

anna: did `docker run --network host` test:
```
Latency   2.9ms    95% 10.1ms   99% 21.0ms
```
anna: Host-networked container is close to host, so bridge/NAT looks like the main offender.

maria: Could be conntrack or Docker's userland-proxy. Check: `sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max` and `ps aux | grep userland-proxy`. Also if conntrack table is thrashing, you'll see drops.

jonathan: Also validate MTU mismatch between VPC overlay and host iface. If packets get fragmented it can cause higher JS latencies. `ip link show` and `ping -M do -s $((1500-28))` quick test.

kevin: Great troubleshooting. Action items:
- anna: open a quick perf ticket with the three wrk outputs + /proc/interrupts + conntrack params (put in eng-runtime board).
- sachin: can you add a brief note on IRQ affinity recommendations for our private image docs?
- maria: check if we should default `--network host` for private low-latency images or recommend disabling userland-proxy in the runtime config.

perf-bot: Scheduled microbench job #pb-18421 on dc2-node-18 (host vs bridge vs host-net-container). Logs: https://bench.redwood/pb-18421 :white_check_mark:

kevin: thanks everyone — if pb-18421 confirms bridge/NAT is the regression we should push a small doc and a config change for private deployments. I'll triage into the sprint. :rocket:
